title: The Three Days Kazuo Inamori Spent Refusing to Promise the Future
conflicts: Headcount: Kyocera's archive says 11 employees; a search summary of Inamori's 2015 Ritsumeikan lecture says 'around ten' (PDF could not be loaded), so the story uses 11 from the archive. Date of the philosophy: Kyocera's chronology dates the management rationale to 1961, its episode and philosophy pages to 1967 after he became president; the story puts the change of view in 1961 and the formal wording in 1967. CSM (1982) gives his founding age as 26; the story does not state it.
notes: The detailed account of the talks (date, 11 people, three days, his home, the leader's tears, both quoted replies) rests on Kyocera's own archive and is attributed to it; Inamori's 2010 Science History Institute oral history (via interpreter) independently confirms the demand for guaranteed livelihoods and the change of purpose. One quoted line ('go ahead and stab me to death') is Kyocera's English translation; the editor may prefer to cut it. Stance 'complicates'.
